rounds.text: Prime Cable Industries Limited is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 24.5 [E1] while delivering explosive growth across multiple timeframes, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 57% [E14] and an astonishing 5-year compounded profit growth of 119% [E17]. This stellar performance is further backed by elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of 42% [E21] and a 5-year ROCE of 27.8% [E12], vastly outperforming the sector median ROCE of 13.4% [E56]. Fundamental intrinsic valuation confirms this mispricing, with a discounted cash flow model placing the intrinsic value at Rs 267 per share against the current market price of Rs 184, providing a substantial 31.1% margin of safety [E37, E38]. Moreover, the reverse DCF indicates that the current price assumes a modest 12.9% earnings growth—well below the 18.0% base case assumption [E39]—while operating margins have expanded by 6 percentage points to reach 10% [E23]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -13 Cr for Mar 2026 resulting in a weak cash conversion of -1.08x [E26, E27], debtor days have increased to 110 days [E45], and institutional money flow shows a negative reading [E36].

Prime Cable Industries Limited exhibits a severe disconnect between its reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of negative ₹13 Cr and a negative free cash flow of ₹34 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28]. This results in a dismal cash conversion ratio of -1.08x, where operating cash flow represents merely -40% of operating profit [E26, E29]. Working capital pressures are intensifying as debtor days have stretched significantly from 87.3 to 110 days [E45], while borrowings have jumped from ₹38 Cr to ₹52 Cr over the last year [E31]. Furthermore, institutional money flow registers as negative, driven by foreign institutions reducing their stake from 2.92% to 1.05% [E34, E36]. The business also fails to reward shareholders, offering a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting profits [E4, E44], and suffers from an alarming return on assets of 0% against a sector benchmark of 8.38% [E8]. Conceded: [E13] and [E17].

While the bear highlights a negative operating cash flow of ₹13 Cr and negative free cash flow of ₹34 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28], this must be weighed against a blistering top-line and bottom-line expansion, including a 5-year compounded profit growth of 119% [E17] and trailing twelve-month sales growth of 67% [E16]. Conceded: debtor days have stretched to 110 days [E45], and borrowings rose to ₹52 Cr [E31], but this comes alongside expanding operating margins that rose from 4% to 10% [E23] and a stellar 3-year median ROE of 42% [E21]. Although foreign institutional holdings decreased [E34], domestic institutions actually increased their stake to 10.81% [E35], demonstrating localized institutional backing. Furthermore, the lack of dividend payout [E4] is typical for hyper-growth companies reinvesting capital to sustain their 36.4% ROE [E13] and 20.45% ROCE [E10]. Finally, the DCF model indicates the intrinsic value sits at ₹267 against a market price of ₹184, providing a solid 31.1% margin of safety [E37, E38].

Conceded: 5-year compounded profit growth is 119% [E17] and trailing twelve-month sales growth is 67% [E16]. However, this rapid top-line expansion has coincided with a severe cash flow disconnect, where operating cash flow is negative at Rs -13 Cr and free cash flow sits at Rs -34 Cr [E27, E28]. Conceded: operating margins expanded by 6 percentage points to 10% and 3-year median ROE is 42% [E21, E23]. Yet, this purported profitability fails to convert into real liquidity, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of -1.08x and debtor days stretching to 110 days [E26, E45]. Furthermore, foreign institutions reduced their stake while overall institutional money flow registers negative [E34, E36], directly undercutting the notion of broad institutional confidence. Finally, borrowings climbed to Rs 52 Cr and the yearly operating margin trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E24, E31], making the growth profile far more fragile than the bull suggests.
